elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend covered claims.
elements.evidence: Both the Servicer and Marketing Agent are expressly required to “defend and indemnify” the Indemnified Persons.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies against covered claims and resulting losses.
elements.evidence: The operative language indemnifies for fees, expenses, losses, claims, actions, suits, damages and liabilities.

elements.element: Customer is an indemnified beneficiary.
elements.evidence: The Issuer, corresponding to Customer, is expressly included as an Indemnified Person.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are indemnified beneficiaries.
elements.evidence: The amendment adds “the Issuer and its Affiliates” to the Indemnified Persons.

elements.element: The indemnity covers third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The coverage of “any claim” and claims, actions and suits is broad enough to include third-party claims, although it is not limited to them.

elements.element: The indemnity covers claims alleging that Vendor-provided services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The added language covers “any claim that any services or deliverables it provides under the Transaction Documents infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.”

elements.element: The indemnity covers claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The added language covers amounts resulting from the applicable indemnitor's “violation of applicable Law.”

elements.element: The indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Coverage is limited to unauthorized access to or disclosure of “Obligor data or Receivable Files.” It does not cover other relevant data or other forms of data breach, such as unauthorized alteration, destruction, loss or acquisition.

elements.element: The indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Both indemnities cover losses resulting from the applicable indemnitor's gross negligence in performing its Transaction Document obligations.

elements.element: The indemnity covers Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Both indemnities cover losses resulting from the applicable indemnitor's willful misconduct in performing its Transaction Document obligations.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure requires Customer to give notice of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: The notice provision expressly applies when indemnity is sought “under this Section 6.3.” The new law, data and IP indemnities are inserted after Section 9.2 rather than within Section 6.3, so the notice procedure does not clearly govern those added claims.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure gives Vendor control of the defense.
elements.evidence: Section 6.3 permits the Servicer or Marketing Agent to assume the defense and settlement, but the added law, data and IP indemnities are placed after Section 9.2 and are not clearly subject to those Section 6.3 mechanics.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure requires reasonable Customer cooperation.
elements.evidence: The operative text states that the Indemnified Person “will provide reasonable cooperation in the defense of the Proceeding.”

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity is limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No Customer or Issuer indemnity is created in the rendered clause. Section 9.2 contains only the Depositor's pre-existing duty to defend title to transferred property against claims through the Depositor, not a Customer indemnity. The limitation condition is therefore satisfied by the demonstrable absence of a Customer indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The added language indemnifies the Indemnified Persons for “any claim” alleging that provided services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights, which includes third-party claims.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for Customer modifications appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications exclusion appears in the operative language.

elements.element: Vendor must have the remedy of procuring continued use of the affected service or deliverable.
elements.evidence: No procure-right remedy appears in the operative language.

elements.element: Vendor must have the remedy of modifying the affected service or deliverable to make it non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy appears in the operative language.

elements.element: Vendor must have the remedy of replacing the affected service or deliverable with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy appears in the operative language.

elements.element: Vendor must provide a refund if the infringement issue cannot be resolved through the other specified remedies.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy appears in the operative language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No liability cap or three-times-annual-fees super-cap appears in the operative text.

result.reason: The redline adds express defense duties, affiliate coverage, and law, data and IP triggers, but it does not fully cover all Vendor-caused data breaches. More importantly, the new trigger language is placed after Section 9.2, while the notice and defense-control mechanics expressly concern claims under Section 6.3, leaving those mechanics inapplicable or materially ambiguous for the new indemnities. The fallback also fails because all stated exclusions, remedies and the 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The redline is not minimal because it reaches neither complete position and extends the new triggers beyond third-party claims. Unrelated existing commercial terms remain operative, so overall intent is preserved despite the placement and scope defects.
